entries.title: LanceDB, which makes a multimodal lakehouse for AI training, built on the open format Lance, raised a $57.5M Series B led by Bessemer and Innovation Endeavors (Kyt Dotson/SiliconANGLE)
Sources: former Nvidia exec Jay Puri, who oversaw chip clients like Alice Huang, controlled chip sales to Super Micro; Puri is married to an ex-Super Micro exec (The Information)
Marco Rubio says there's "zero evidence" linking the recent FAA ground stop, Microsoft outage, and bank service issues, and the US isn't "under systemic attack" (Kiki Intarasuwan/CBS News)
Sources: a faction of Nvidia board members is pushing for Jensen Huang's return despite Chair Harvey Jones stating the board has no plans to reinstate Huang (Semafor)
After two months of testimony, the US criminal trial against Huawei, accused of bank fraud and trade secret theft, is set to begin jury deliberations Wednesday (Karen Freifeld/Reuters)
Analysis: San Francisco-based AI startup insiders hold a combined $1.2T in equity; at Anthropic's IPO midpoint, the average employee's equity is valued at $72M (Bloomberg)
Sources: Wall Street execs and the NSA told Congress this week's outages stemmed from systems overwhelmed by a rush to patch vulnerabilities found by AI models (Jeff Stein/The Washington Sun)
Tech outages disrupting everything from air travel to banking transactions over the past week have fueled public distrust and paranoia about tech infrastructure (Bloomberg)
FAA pauses installations of Juniper routers like the one officials believe contributed to Friday's nationwide ground stop; HPE says its device wasn't defective (Neil Vigdor/New York Times)
Colette Kress says Nvidia will no longer sell H200 chips in China, ending its role in a deal brokered by Huang and Trump that let the US collect a 25% tariff (Tim Fernholz/TechCrunch)
Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress says the company will stay "disciplined and selective" in supporting neoclouds; CoreWeave and Nebius jump 9%+ after hours (Ina Fried/Axios)
Apple HomeView teardown: a step backward in repairability compared to recent iPads and HomePods, with heavily glued display, speakers, and logic board (Carsten Frauenheim/iFixit News)
Sources detail how the Microsoft 365 outage began in Switzerland and spread as failover systems shifted traffic, leaving 80%+ of Exchange servers unresponsive (Tom Warren/The Verge)
On Q3 earnings call, Nvidia Chair Harvey Jones says the board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO (Hayden Field/The Verge)
Suno launches Visuals, letting users generate 15-second clips that can be spliced into a full music video, using a MiniMax-based model; video credits cost extra (Ashley Carman/Bloomberg)
